notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 86 this time, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

- **First attempt:** I tried to open six pages directly: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Gill and Ellicott on BibleHub, Augustine's exposition on New Advent, and the NET Bible notes. All six were refused, because the tool only opens addresses that have first come up in a search.
- **Second attempt:** I then ran the searches to get those addresses, but the system had run out of tool calls for this turn. They didn't run.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. With no pages read, that means leaving everything out. I could have written notes from what I already know about these commentators, but they wouldn't be sourced, so I haven't.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with searches and then open the pages they return. The plan:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon on BibleHub or StudyLight.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** likely v. 2 ("I am godly") and v. 11 ("undivided heart"). I'd check Reformed, Wesleyan, Lutheran and Baptist teachers on those to see whether they really read them differently.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes for modern scholarship. Augustine on New Advent for the Catholic reading; he numbers this Psalm 85, following the Greek Old Testament's numbering. OCA for the Orthodox reading. I'd only include prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching if the allowed sites actually discuss this psalm.
